Each not-yet-embedded URL therefore triggers a full feed fetch+parse on the worker. The behavior isn't broken (throttled to 60s per URL), but the redundant full-feed re-fetch per URL is a real, specific scalability/load concern grounded in this diff that a maintainer would want to know — a substantive review concern, not a defect.

judged_text: perform_retrieve synchronously executes the entire PollFeed job (`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`), re-fetching and re-parsing the whole RSS feed, once per each not-yet-embedded URL requested. A site embedding N new pages within an hour triggers N full feed fetches on Sidekiq workers — multiplying outbound load against the feed host and delaying each retrieve job by the full feed parse time.

A site embedding N new pages within an hour triggers N full feed fetches on Sidekiq workers — multiplying outbound load against the feed host and delaying each retrieve job by the full feed parse time.

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/topic_retriever.rb` `perform_retrieve` does `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` synchronously does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates all items. Since `perform_retrieve` is invoked per `@embed_url` (via `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`), each not-yet-embedded URL can trigger a full feed fetch/parse, multiplying outbound requests and increasing retrieve latency. This is a performance/architecture concern rather than a functional defect.
